# jamfplatform_pro_restricted_software (Data Source)

Look up a Jamf Pro restricted software record by ID or by exact name. Exactly one of `id` or `name` must be supplied. Surfaces a flat read-only projection; manage the record as a resource for full detail.

**Required Jamf permissions**

Grant the API integration the following permissions in Jamf Account. `Category` and `Permission` name the section and row of the permission picker; `Actions` are the boxes to tick within that row.

| Category | Permission | Actions | API capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| App lifecycle management | Restricted software | Read | `restricted-software` |

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up a restricted software record by exact name.
data "jamfplatform_pro_restricted_software" "by_name" {
  name = "Block Chess"
}

output "block_chess_id" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_restricted_software.by_name.id
}

# Look up a restricted software record by ID.
data "jamfplatform_pro_restricted_software" "by_id" {
  id = "10"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Record ID. Mutually exclusive with `name`.
- `name` (String) Display name (exact match). Mutually exclusive with `id`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `delete_application` (Boolean) Whether the application running the restricted process is deleted.
- `display_message` (String) Message displayed to users when the process is found.
- `kill_process` (Boolean) Whether the restricted process is terminated.
- `process_name` (String) The restricted process name.
- `restrict_exact_process_name` (Boolean) Whether only the exact process name is restricted.
- `send_email_notification_on_violation` (Boolean) Whether an email notification is sent on violation.
- `site_id` (String) Site ID. `-1` means no site.
- `site_name` (String) Site display name.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
